Landing hero composition
The landing page shows the wordmark, the published headline, sentence and Open your deck action on the left, and the pinned wine-coloured field with the demo tile on the right, as described in Visual design.

Landing demo reel
The landing tile plays the three bundled demo stops through the fader, and scrolling the left column and moving the fader drive each other as described in Interactions.

Bundled demo stops
Landing always plays exactly the three bundled demo stops in seed order, with the seed's names, makers, years, millimetre size lines and computed swatches, announced in the published wording, whatever happens to the Demo reel or its references and whether or not storage is reachable.

Saved only once confirmed
A capture answers 201 only after storage confirms the byte-exact original and, while search is up, the search index confirms the document, and a failed capture leaves no row, search document, tile or stored object.

Photo type and size from its bytes
Capture decides JPEG or PNG from the photo's bytes, names the stored original and reports its content type to match, rejects photos that are neither type with 422, and rejects photos over the pixel limit with 422 from their header dimensions within the published time and before any pixel is decoded or anything is stored, as qualified in Business rules.

Capture validation
Capture rejects invalid fields with 422 and the per-field copy from Feedback states, and rejects oversize bodies with 413, as qualified in API.

Idempotency keys
A repeated request with the same idempotency key and content returns the first success without repeating its effect, the same key with different content returns 409, a duplicate that arrives on any app copy while the first is still in progress returns 409 `idempotency_in_flight`, each key is scoped to its method and path, and no error answer is ever recorded against a key.

Capture journey
On a phone the designer takes or picks a photo, fills in the facts and saves, then sees the published success copy and the new reference at the top of Saved today.

Saved today in the home zone
The library groups stored references into Saved today and Earlier, using the day boundary in Business rules from the effective home zone on the server's clock, whatever zone or clock the browser has.

Confirmed search
Search queries the search index over the published fields and filters, a newly captured or restored reference is findable as soon as its write answers, and a trashed or purged one is gone as soon as its write answers.

Latest search wins
The library shows only the results for the latest search text and filter, even when an older search answers last, and reports the settled result count in the published words.

Browse journey
Focusing or hovering a library row loads that reference into the tile, and opening the row shows its facts view.

True sizes without drift
Sizes are stored once as whole tenths of a millimetre and shown and printed in millimetres or inches to one decimal place by one rule, and saving an unchanged inch value never changes the stored size.

Original kept, pixels upright
The stored and downloaded original is byte for byte the uploaded file, while the swatch, the eyedropper, the display crop and the pixel limit all work on the upright image its orientation tag describes.

Swatch and eyedropper
Each reference's swatch is computed once from its stored original as a screen colour by the published rule, converting wide-gamut phone photos and leaving out fully transparent pixels, the eyedropper overrides it from a point by pointer, touch or keyboard, Reset swatch returns the computed colour, and the tile and contact sheet use the stored swatch.

Facts version conflict
A facts edit must carry the reference's current version, of two edits sent on the same version to any app copies exactly one succeeds and the other returns 409 and changes nothing, and the losing window shows the published copy and reloads the facts.

Facts and original journey
From the library the designer opens a reference's facts, switches the size unit and opens the uncropped original with one key press.

Fader detents
The reel fader is a slider with one numbered detent per playable stop, values 0 to N-1, operated by arrow keys, Home, End, drag, tap and the published bracket shortcuts.

Fader Pull sequence
Each stop change runs the published steps in order, with value, address and scroll first, then the shutter closing as the swatch crossfades, then the shutter opening on the new photo, name and size, with timings and the release settle as in Motion and effects, and a change arriving mid-swap ends the running swap at once so the tile settles on the newest stop and nothing from an older stop is painted afterwards.

Scroll-bound fader
Scrolling the reel column moves the fader through the stops in step with the scroll in both directions, and moving the fader scrolls the column to that stop's row.

Reel announcer
Every user-driven stop change, and every swap forced by a refetch, is announced once in a polite live region with the published wording from Feedback states.

Stop kept through refetch
The Reel screen refetches on load, every 60 seconds and on window focus, keeps the fader on the same reference without a swap while it is playable, and moves to a neighbouring stop with one announced swap when it is not.

Stop in the address
The Reel screen's address carries the current stop as a 1-based stop number, so reloading reopens the same stop without a swap, and an invalid number opens stop 1.

Keyboard reel playback
The designer plays a seeded reel from first to last stop and back using only the keyboard, with visible focus throughout and no focus trap.

Reel stops
Reels keep an ordered list of stops that can be appended to, reordered and removed through the API, and trashed stops stay in place but are skipped in playback and printing.

One winner per reel write
Of reorders sent on the same reel version, of appends racing for the last free stop, and of appends of the same reference, exactly one succeeds across every app copy sharing the database and every other returns its published 409 and changes nothing.

Honest reorder
A moved stop shows in its new place at once, moves made while one is pending are sent in order each with the version from the previous answer, a refused move returns the list to the server's last accepted order with the published copy, and the success copy appears only after the server accepts.

Keyboard reorder journey
The designer moves a stop up and down with its move buttons, and the new order persists after a reload.

Sheet states and storage
A contact sheet moves from queued to rendering to ready or failed, a failed sheet can be retried with exactly one winner among simultaneous retries, it prints the reel's playable stops as they were when requested, and it is ready only after its PDF is stored and read back byte for byte.

Sheet PDF content
The PDF uses the requested paper size and the published page layout and footer, and shows each stop's embedded photo, position, name, maker, year, size in the chosen unit and swatch.

Nothing private on the sheet
No sheet snapshot, PDF or HTML sent for rendering contains a reference's notes, source link or where-found note, and no display crop or sheet carries any of the original photograph's embedded metadata.

Print journey
The designer prints a reel as a contact sheet, watches its state reach Ready and downloads the PDF.

Trash and restore transitions
Trashing and restoring follow the published state machine, return 409 for each illegal transition, and hide trashed references from the library, search and Daily Pull.

Exact restore
A restored reference comes back with the same id, capture time, swatch and swatch source, reel positions and full search document, and a restored day's pick is again that day's Daily Pull.

Restore window and countdown
A trashed reference can be restored up to and including the end of its retention period and is then purged everywhere with the published refusal, as qualified in Business rules, and Trash shows the server's remaining time whatever the device clock.

Trash journey
Using the keyboard, the designer moves a reference to the trash through a confirmation dialog, finds it in the trash with its countdown and restores it.

Daily Pull pick
Each pull day the server picks one stored reference by the published rule, excluding the last 30 pulls, every request that day on every app copy returns the same single pick, and trashing the pick never triggers a new pick that day.

Daily Pull rollover
The pull day turns over at 06:00 local in the effective home zone by the server's clock, including across a clock change, and the card shows the server's pull with its date in the published format whatever the browser's clock, zone or language.

Daily Pull card journey
The library's Daily Pull card shows the current pick with its date and next pull time, and opening the card shows the pick's facts.

Home zone change at midnight
Only zone names from the published zone list are accepted, a new home zone takes effect at the next true local midnight in the old zone, including across a clock change, and until then Daily Pull, Saved today and the current year keep using the old zone.

Settings journey
The designer picks a new home zone and a size unit on Settings and sees the published notice with the moment the change takes effect.

Boot and self-recovery
The app starts and serves every screen while search, storage or printing is unreachable, shows each service's published banner, and clears it and resumes deferred work within the published delays when the service returns, without a restart.

Storage outage leaves nothing behind
While storage is unreachable, captures and swatch changes return 503 and leave nothing stored, the capture form keeps everything entered, and the same idempotency key succeeds once storage returns.

Search fallback and catch-up
While search is unreachable or its index is being rebuilt, search answers from the library's own records under the published banner, references changed meanwhile become searchable in order within the catch-up delay once search returns, and a lost index is recreated and rebuilt from the library's records within the published delay.

Printing waits in the queue
While printing is unreachable, sheet requests are accepted and stay queued under the published banner, and they render once printing returns.

Published layouts
At 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 each screen shows its published layout and order, with no horizontal scrolling.

Touch and reduced motion
Capture, the fader and the eyedropper work by touch with the target sizes from Visual design, and with reduced motion every swap is instant and works the same way.

Keyboard and dialogs
Every action works by keyboard with visible focus, and each dialog keeps Tab inside it, closes on Escape and returns focus to the control that opened it.

Visual direction
Every screen carries the nocturnal hero-object look described in Visual design.

Server boundary
The server accepts same-origin requests only, enforces body limits, never serves source files or credentials, and keeps the browser away from the backing services.

Real integrations from configuration
Every service is reached with the credentials and URLs from its environment variables, and every saved, indexed or printed state comes from the real provider, never from a stand-in.

Capture progress announced
Pressing Save to deck shows the published pending copy and marks the button busy before any answer arrives, then shows exactly one result message that no later refetch or status check overwrites, and a refused capture marks each invalid field and moves focus to the first one in the published form order.

Library updates in place
A library refetch adds, updates and removes rows in place, keeps the focused row, the tile and any active search exactly as they were, and never writes to Deck status.

Tile slide
On every stop change the new stop's photo slides horizontally into its resting place during the second half of the Fader Pull, from the right when moving forward and from the left when moving back, as in Motion and effects.

Screen slide
Following a link in the Deck navigation slides the new screen's main content in from the side of travel while the navigation and the field stay put, and a screen opened by its address appears without a slide.

Dialog slide
Every dialog slides up into place as it opens and back down as it closes, with focus moving inside at once, as in Motion and effects.

Row slide
Reel rows that change place slide to their new positions instead of jumping, and a row leaving a list slides out to the left before the rows below close the gap, as in Motion and effects.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve fields and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and its serve command starts the app.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at the root of /app lists every shipped package with its licence, and every font and demo photograph with its source and licence. Shipped packages are the production dependency tree, as reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.

Shipped packages (the production dependency tree, as reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) use only MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or 0BSD licences. Fonts use OFL-1.1. Demo photographs are CC0 or drawn for this product.
The only datastores are Postgres, MinIO and Meilisearch. No SQLite, embedded key-value store, in-memory store standing in for a service, or local files hold application state.
The provided service configuration and its development credentials are left untouched.
Server and browser source is TypeScript.
Icons come from the Lucide icon set.
